Sample review, 2026-10-24

Evidence directory:
/usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-28a4cdc2/scratch/triage

No sample executable was run. atomscan and cleave facts were run on all three
originals. ILSpy decompilation, dnfile CLR-resource inspection, Inno extraction,
IFPS disassembly, signature verification and read-only endpoint retrieval were
used to verify the findings. Decoded string facts were reviewed alongside code.

96082e1bb5350495ce83fe6ad1c26cfde4c31171c0f200bc68585d2d08f3d9ef
Identity: Ultimate Metin2 / Ultimate Gems Cloud WinForms game launcher.
Disposition: BENIGN, with the corpus-provenance caveat that this is an assessment
of the recovered artifact, not proof of every deployment or future update.

launcher.cs contains the complete decompilation (301 managed methods). Main
starts the visible launcher, or explicitly requested preview/self-test/update/
recovery modes. PlayGame launches executor.exe from the selected game directory.
CheckUpdate calls UpdateCore.Prepare, copies its own image to GemsUpdateApply.exe,
then launches that helper with --apply and a plan path. The helper waits for its
parent before replacing files; rollback/recovery restore local backup copies.
CreateNoWindow belongs to these helper launches, not a hidden command shell.
Registry access stores UI preferences under HKCU Software/UltimateMetin2/
GemsLauncher, not an autorun key. ApprovedLink limits browser links to configured
HTTPS community/game sites. Assembly resource reads supply images and JSON,
not Assembly.Load, injected code, or reflection-driven execution.

Prepare reads local gems_update.json, requires HTTPS without redirects or URL
credentials, retrieves Builds/latest-v2.json and its manifest, validates SHA256
and lengths, checks free space and whether the game is closed, and stages allowed
game files. Local rejects traversal, rooted paths, reserved DOS devices, trailing
spaces/dots and reparse points. RuntimePath excludes account/password/credential
files, screenshots, logs and user data. The credential-related strings describe
preservation boundaries and tests, not credential harvesting. COM1..COM9 are
reserved names in that path validator; their literal-reference observation is
retained and its description now explicitly mentions reserved COM names.

All twelve managed resources are expected PNG images or JSON catalogs. Every PNG
ends at IEND with zero trailing bytes. PNG compression explains the enormous
near-random .text/CLR-resource measurements; these accurate entropy observations
remain. The image also contains C2PA metadata, not a network payload.

Retrieved the configured launcher.json, latest-v2.json and the referenced
manifest from patch.ultimatemt2.com. The manifest's launcher SHA256 is exactly the
original sample hash; downloading GemsCloudLauncher.exe independently reproduced
that hash. Retrieved the game executor, GeoAudio helper, endpoint INI and update
configuration and checked their manifest hashes. executor.exe is a native Metin2
client with Direct3D/Python/game functionality and named anti-cheat classes.
Process-inspection API references in that client are not attributed to this
launcher. GeoAudio was fully decompiled: a pinned-certificate HTTPS POST sends
version, an ephemeral session identifier and a client label; its bounded JSON
response supplies country/language/IP for local audio-language cache files. It
has no microphone recording or arbitrary response-code execution. The original
launcher carries no embedded update-channel configuration beyond referenced
local files, so the deployment's actual sidecar settings remain unknown.

The balance of verified game-updater behavior, private-file exclusions and exact
publisher-hosted byte match supports BENIGN. The missing signature, blank version
fields, huge compressed resources and self-copy/update-helper launches plausibly
explain generic ML detections and corpus collection. The source's exact reason
and the user's authorization on any historical machine are unavailable.

8c35b7d47f65832206369e00760fea41bf20e023596cd2dad966d02bafa93151
Identity: Softonic_DLM / Softonic_2 Inno Setup 6.7 offer-bundle downloader.
Disposition: MALICIOUS in the requested binary scheme: unwanted distribution
software warranting quarantine. This does not label its partner products malware.

osslsigncode verifies the Authenticode content digest, certificate chain,
countersignature and CRLs, signed as SOFTONIC INTERNATIONAL SA on 2026-09-09.
The PE checksum is nonstandard but the signed bytes are intact. GETUFID uses that
checksum as a fallback configuration/download ID (208130476, padded 0208130476),
so its mismatch is not evidence of post-signing tampering.

The installed innoextract rejects the revised loader/setup data. Fetched upstream
inno-6.4-to-6.7-support through forager and built it in scratch. Instrumented only
that analysis build to save the original compiled_code bytes. It recovered four
UI assets and the full PascalScript; Binary Refinery's IFPS disassembler produced
softonic.ifps.txt. Original sample bytes were unchanged.

InitializeSetup sets Softonic/Softonic_DLM/Softonic_2. GETREMOTEJSON creates
WinHttp.WinHttpRequest.5.1 and POSTs GETREQUESTPOSTDATA to a configured CloudFront
/o URL. INITMAINCARRIER reads remote carrier title/URL/filename/arguments.
INITPRODS parses offer configuration and eligibility checks (architecture,
installed apps/registry/processes, browser, disk/RAM, geography, and recent
antivirus-uninstall state). These are offer-targeting checks; they do not establish
sandbox evasion, credential theft or disabling antivirus.

CurPageChanged -> SHOWDNLDPAGE -> DNLDFILE downloads the carrier/selected offers.
TDownloadWizardPage.Add is given an empty required SHA256 argument. INSTALLPRODS
checks file magic, handles ZIP extraction/executable selection, and calls
ShellExec with remotely supplied arguments. SENDREPORT transmits installation
and campaign events with user/session/platform identifiers. GETUSERID reads
MachineGuid; Slack registry inventory is also present. Offer UI and selection
state exist: lack of consent is not invented from silent-install arguments.

A read-only POST using synthetic OS/language values and this artifact's checksum
ID returned Grand Theft Auto 5 Theme as carrier plus six partner offers: Avast
One, OperaGX, Opera, AVG Anti Virus, Avast Secure Browser and CCleaner. Their
commands include /silent, --silent and advertising identifiers. A partner ZIP was
retrieved through forager and its executable signature verifies. The carrier's
expiring signed URL returned HTTP 412. The supplied Triage page was inaccessible
to the web tool; no sandbox-only behavior became a static claim. Historical
responses, installation completion, user selections and the landing-page consent
flow are missing context. Remote control over partner installation plus targeted
commercial offers/tracking and the supplied PUA provenance tip the disposition
toward unwanted software, not a commodity Trojan inferred from reputation alone.

Coverage limitation: zero hostile and one independent suspicious family finding
before and after. That family finding is accurate and remains suspicious. The
substantive offer-request/targeting, downloaded-installer execution and tracking
paths are in compressed PascalScript that the installed scanner cannot expose.
The recovered IFPS file has unknown file type in cleave facts. YAML cannot decode
Inno's LZMA/IFPS representation or truthfully claim those effects from ordinary
Inno imports. The newer extractor and disassembly close the analysis gap, not the
scanner's extraction gap. No extra family aliases, entropy convictions, or
unsupported hostile rules were added to approach a numerical trait target.

8128514a9917b6dcdf20f7ee24d6b00a27b2a6aa0f971acb988f358f25ac4005
Identity: a 332-byte HTML HTTP 502 Server Error response.
Disposition: BENIGN. The complete file contains a title, content-type meta tag,
body headings, colors and retry text. It has no script, URL, dependency, form,
redirect, encoded stage or executable content. Its hash matches the supplied
content SHA256; the long filename is a different digest. A failed fetch saved
under an expected payload's name is the likely collection explanation. The
intended original payload or URL is unavailable and is not assessed as benign.
No new trait is justified for a plain error page.

Rule corrections, with unsupported claims and retained coverage

* unsigned-dll-data-extension-structure previously matched the launcher EXE
  because dll shares PE analysis scope. Require the parsed PE DLL characteristic.
  Actual EXE and DLL-header variants are both tested; severity is unchanged.
* Bare Guarda matched Portuguese bodyguard/town-guard content. Match the common
  language suffix as part of evidence before applying span-level exclusions.
  Standalone wallet brands and a real Salat stealer still match; a mixed
  language/real-wallet fixture confirms exclusions cannot hide another brand.
* SHA256 in Inno is a native implementation/module name, not a .NET type.
  Rename the canonical reference and description without changing its matcher
  or severity. Update its consumer and the existing twelve managed controls.
* Opaque filename plus FNV constant proves a checksum/name observation; opaque
  filename plus OriginalFilename mismatch proves a provenance relation. Move
  both out of payload staging at the same notable criticality with identical
  scope and matchers; omit unsupported inherited execution ATT&CK mappings.
  Preserve hosts-file and CrystalX ancestor selectors through exact references;
  CrystalX's existing exception group preserves its original OR semantics.
  The Python-only dynamic-dropper selector cannot consume either PE-only rule.
* A resource updater-label matcher does not prove a VERSIONINFO field. Move it
  to resource/identity, preserving matcher/scope/severity and its exact consumer.
  Audit provenance ancestors: ELF-only consumers cannot match it. Two mixed-PE
  hidden-path downgrade consumers explicitly retain the relocated observation;
  fixtures verify unchanged downgrades. No directory limit was raised.
* Add notable code-section GetFinalPathNameByHandle and structured A/W import
  observations under filesystem path normalization. Validation exposed unused
  suffixed API names in a minimal Go runtime; those names alone are excluded
  by evidence scope, without a Go-wide exception or severity reduction.

No hostile or suspicious rule was removed, weakened or suppressed. The launcher
loses the two incorrect notable findings, while its SHA256 and filename facts
remain under corrected IDs and the new path API is detected. The engine also
prunes the now-unused baseline pe-sparse-import-table helper after the incorrect
DLL composite stops firing; the stronger existing single-import finding and
facts still report the one CLR import. This is no attack-coverage loss.

The Softonic ML verdict disagrees with the unwanted-software disposition even
though its accurate suspicious family finding remains. This classifier miss is
reported rather than repaired by invented hostile traits. Model v18 also warns
that the engine has newer features (v21); model retraining is outside YAML scope.

All sixteen extracted resource/installer members were scanned against the HEAD
rules snapshot and edited rules: zero hostile/suspicious findings in both runs.
The original scanner exposes no archive-member tree for unsupported Inno data.
Original bytes, manual extraction and their separate findings are distinguished.

through forager with Hopper provenance. Compared full atomscan reports using a

The original Salat finding set is preserved; unused runtime API names do not

controls pass. check.py exercises production matching (rather than test-rules,
